implReport.summary:
Resumed after restart 9 (05:29 UTC) and closed the task. The final tree is the live src/sim, a copy of which is frozen at /home/user/frozen-openingfix2. It is the close sweep's tree (9a8cdf07) plus one new fix ("fix 5"). Integrator ruling 3 led to it: the unplug draft (allocation/unplugDraft.ts) used to draft workers up to the whole dig target, which includes the founding plan's demand. So at every hand-over it pulled foragers into digging for about 700 ticks. It now drafts only up to the floor's own shortfall. Run from the close sweep's 15 hand-overs, the final tree gives 15 of 15 viable and 264 workers at winter; the close sweep had 12 of 15 and 249 on the same hand-overs. The integrator's floor-off arm also gave 15 / 264, so the fix recovers the whole cost while keeping the floor.

Browser, firstplay.mjs: beats 01-13 pass with no stand-ins on seeds 1-5, on both the close tree and the final tree.

R14 (entrance open within 4 game hours of the hand-over) is missed only on cold-night hand-overs. A trace shows the cause is the work rate: diggers at 10-13 C work at 0.24-0.43 of full rate, and they never stop. Counted at full work rate, seed 4 opens after 1.7 hours. I proposed a restatement of R14 on that basis (ruling 2).

Ruling 3 (a): the player's 4 first workers come from a 12-egg clutch. Base brood mortality kills 8 of the 12, which matches the on-screen forecast "First workers 3-5". The clutch is 12 eggs because the script's layBatch pressed while a 58-tick batch was still running, so every other press was refused 'blocked'. Look-pass-6 has since fixed layBatch.

Full runs, first failure after beat 13, none of them a hand-over defect of the kind this task fixes, so none fixed:
- Close tree: seed 1 stops at 13->14 (no trail; 4 workers lay too little scent); seed 2 at 15->16 (the larder cap R21(b) refuses the delivery).
- Final tree with the new script: seed 1 reaches beat 19 with 14 workers and stops at 19->20 (the colony-view dig planner refuses the anchor, 'anchor-not-in-nest'); seed 2 stops at 13->14 (no linked trail; the larder is full, so the colony's sugar need is 0).

Item 5 is met on both trees: the five paired sweep-15 hand-overs are 5 of 5 viable. Long runs on the final tree: 90 -> 113 workers, R22 5/5, R34 at 1.0x 4/5.

Ruling 2's cavity-only mound-mask arm was not better overall, so nothing changed for it.

findings.title: The headless opening kit no longer issues the browser script's lay commands
findings.detail: playerOpeningKit.ts still presses lay-egg, steps 50, releases, then steps 5. At the cell's 17 C a batch takes 58 ticks, so every second press is refused 'blocked' and the kit lays 2 batches (12 eggs). The file header claims 'four lay batches'. firstplay.mjs (look-pass-6) now waits for action-completed / action-failed and lays 4 batches (24 eggs). Spec item 2 says the headless script drives 'the same commands as beats 04-13', and that is no longer true. playerOpening.long.test.ts and tools/sim/opening.ts therefore guard a 12-egg opening the browser no longer plays. Fix: port the new layBatch (poll the event log for the lay-egg action's end) into the kit, then re-run playerOpening.long. The 4-worker case is still worth keeping as an explicit extra case.

findings.title: Unplug stand-point lockout found but left in place, against ruling 2
findings.detail: The stand point is placed e.radius + UNPLUG_STAND_BU down the throat axis. When the mouth is wide this lies inside the plug, so a digger coming up from the cell fails approach() at once and is barred from unplugging for 600 ticks. The implementer's own trace shows it (test-output/opening-fix/headless/trace-s4.txt; trace-s4-stand.txt for the reverted prototype): the second digger reaches the plug at +719 instead of +103. Ruling 2 says 'If something else holds them (no digger allocated at night, a rest rule), fix that.' The report defers it because the measured gain to open time was only 5 % (1287 -> 1224 ticks). The defect is real and inside the task's owned paths. The integrator should either have it fixed or accept the deferral explicitly.

findings.title: The long test checks R14 on headless hand-overs that are not the browser's failing case
findings.detail: Seeds 1 and 2 are held to R14 (1000 ticks), but headless they hand over 13 and 11 workers; the browser seeds that failed had 4 and 7. The only 4-worker case (seed 4) is held to 7500 ticks, 7.5 times R14. Seed 2 opens at exactly 1000 ticks on a 250-tick poll, so any change that adds one poll turns the test red even if the cause is unrelated. The regression guard against 'no digger for the plug' therefore only proves 'eventually' for the small colony. Suggest a tighter seed-4 bound once R14's restatement is ruled, for example the measured 1287-1500 ticks plus margin.

findings.title: R14 (open within 4 game hours of the hand-over) is still unmet on cold-night hand-overs
findings.detail: Browser seeds 1, 2 and 4 open 5-7 game hours after a 12-15 C night hand-over. I confirmed this on seed 2's picture 13: hand-over 19:46, open entrance at 02:46. The report's work-rate table (digrate-s4.txt) supports cold work rate as the main cause, apart from the stand-point lockout above. Ruling 2 foresaw this case and allowed a restatement, but it has not been ruled yet. Recorded so the integrator rules on the proposed restatement; it is not an implementation defect.
